title: S4 · Does backing or fading home-nation players make money?

hypothesis.statement: Players from the tournament's host country win at a rate different from their no-vig market price, and backing or fading them earns a positive ROI.
hypothesis.rationale: Home crowds, local-media attention and bettors backing their compatriots could push home players' prices below fair — or crowd support could genuinely help them and the market under-price it. Either direction is testable.
hypothesis.metric: home-player win rate vs market-implied (z-test); ROI and CLV bootstrap 95% CIs of back_home_nation and fade_home_nation
hypothesis.threshold: Supported iff the cohort p < 0.05 and a strategy's 2019+ ROI CI lies entirely above 0 with >= 100 bets.
hypothesis.out_of_sample: seasons >= 2019, reported alongside the full sample

plain_title: Do players win more at home than the odds expect?
plain_summary: We check whether players from the country hosting a tournament win more or less often than the bookmakers' odds imply, and whether betting on them (or against them) would have made money.
